stories.headline: Update: Britain Blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for Suspected Plot Against RAF Fairford Base
stories.summary:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the House of Commons on Monday that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was "almost certainly" behind a suspected plot to attack RAF Fairford, the base where U.S. bombers have been stationed. "I can confirm our assessment that it is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by the IRGC," he said.

It is the first time the British government has officially attributed the alleged planned attack to Iran. Burnham said the United Kingdom would not tolerate such threats. The claim comes as the U.S.-Iran war continues and as Iran has described the latest U.S. proposal to end the fighting as "insufficient."

The attribution raises the prospect of further British involvement in the wider conflict and adds to regional tension, which includes repeated Houthi strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. Further details of the alleged plot, including any arrests or evidence, were not set out in the available reporting. The announcement is likely to prompt questions about security at bases used by U.S. forces in Britain and about how London responds diplomatically.

stories.headline: Update: Russia Keeps Striking Ukrainian Energy Sites Despite Trump's Announced 'Energy Ceasefire'
stories.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday that Russia has continued to strike Ukraine's energy infrastructure, in violation of what President Trump declared a day earlier to be an energy ceasefire agreed by both countries. Zelensky said Russian forces hit a thermal power plant in Kharkiv and other energy facilities. Trump had written on social media: "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!"

Zelensky initially expressed surprise at the announcement, then said Ukraine would support a truce if Moscow does, calling it "good news for everyone." He noted that Russian "shaheds," or attack drones, filled Ukrainian skies. Trump made a similar announcement a month ago, after which both sides continued aerial attacks on each other's energy facilities.

Separately, a bipartisan group of six senators, four Republicans and two Democrats, called on the administration to "immediately reverse course" on a plan to buy Russian diesel to lower fuel prices. They said the White House failed to consult Congress or provide the explanation required by statute. Trump has also reportedly threatened to block a procurement system supplying weapons to Ukraine if it continues striking Russian energy infrastructure.

stories.headline: Update: Trump Privately Doubts Livestreaming Fort Hood Gunman's Execution as Al Qaeda Issues Threat
stories.summary:
President Trump has privately expressed misgivings about livestreaming the firing-squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the former Army major who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009, according to four people who have spoken with him. A senior administration official said Trump has been deluged with "negative input" from a bipartisan group of lawmakers and from advisers inside and outside the White House.

Trump had said he approved of a livestream but suggested the decision might not be final. Republicans and Vice President Vance had earlier pushed back on the idea. The execution would be the first time the U.S. Army has used a firing squad since 1945.

The new development Monday is a threat from Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula, which said it would execute any U.S. nationals it kidnaps if the government carries out Hasan's scheduled execution. The group said in a statement that this would happen "the day America makes this decision." The threat adds a security dimension to a debate that had centered on whether broadcasting a state execution is appropriate.

stories.headline: Elon Musk Becomes Biggest Known Midterm Donor With More Than $276 Million for Republicans
stories.summary:
Elon Musk has quietly become the largest known donor in this year's midterm elections, giving more than $276 million since July to help Republicans keep their congressional majorities. The figures were first reported by The New York Times ahead of this week's federal filing deadline and confirmed by Andrew Romeo, a spokesperson for Musk's super PAC.

The total includes $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund, one of the largest known political donations in American history, and $76 million to America PAC, which has rebuilt a turnout operation like the one used to help elect Trump in 2024. Musk also gave $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, which backs Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton in Texas.

The spending reverses Musk's statement last May that he had "done enough" and would cut back. Despite his lower public profile, he has reconciled with Trump after a falling out over leaving his government role. Republicans hold a large financial advantage over Democrats, a rare bright spot for a party bracing for potential losses amid voter frustration over prices, the president's performance and the unpopular war with Iran. Democrats are expected to win the House, with some chance at the Senate, 22 days before the election.

stories.headline: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home in immigration probe
stories.summary:
Federal agents conducted a pre-dawn search Monday at the Washington home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) as part of an ongoing criminal investigation connected to immigration, a Justice Department spokesperson confirmed. Agents from Homeland Security Investigations, the investigative arm of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, carried out the search. Fox News first reported the operation and posted video that appeared to show law enforcement officers in HSI jackets outside the residence.

The search marks a significant escalation in the Trump administration's scrutiny of the Minnesota Democrat, an outspoken progressive who has condemned the immigration crackdown in her state. Officials have not publicly detailed the nature of the investigation, what was sought, or whether Omar herself is a target. The Justice Department described the action as an enforcement action tied to an ongoing probe.

The administration and its supporters have generally framed such investigations as routine law enforcement that applies to any official, regardless of party or office. Critics, including many Democrats, are likely to view the search of a sitting member of Congress who has opposed administration policy as politically charged and to press for details on the legal basis for the warrant. Omar has been among the most prominent critics of immigration enforcement.

The search drew coverage from Axios, Bloomberg, NBC, The Hill, Fox News and The Guardian. Further details, including any response from Omar or congressional leaders and any court filings related to the warrant, are expected to emerge in the coming days.

stories.headline: Update: Indian opposition leaders march to Supreme Court demanding election chief's resignation
stories.summary:
India's opposition parties marched through central Delhi on Monday to the Supreme Court to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter fraud. Thousands of security personnel were deployed, roads were barricaded, and entry and exit at some metro stations was restricted. Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, who called on all opposition parties and civil society groups to join, rode in a bus at the head of the march, alongside student leader Neha Bora.

Opposition parties allege that under Kumar, voter rolls are being manipulated to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party, particularly through a contentious revision of electoral rolls. Both the Election Commission and the BJP reject the charge. Gandhi and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to Chief Justice Surya Kant laying out their concerns.

The Chief Justice declined to meet the opposition lawmakers, citing unspecified reasons; media reports say he noted some issues were already pending before the court. He said every citizen has the right to approach the court and that it would hear their concerns. Gandhi said Kant had asked them to file a petition, which they planned to do at the end of the march.

The march follows a week of protests in Delhi in which top opposition leaders, including Gandhi, were briefly detained several times, and a weekend in which thousands of demonstrators from the Cockroach Janata Party pressure group were detained. That group, not a registered political party, has said it will keep protesting until Kumar steps down.

stories.headline: Two U.S. economists win Nobel Prize in economics for work on stabilizing economies
stories.summary:
Stanford University's Robert E. Hall and Columbia University's Michael Woodford won the Nobel Prize in economics, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced Monday. The academy honored their research on models that help governments and central banks manage economic shocks and smooth boom-and-bust cycles to limit unemployment and inflation.

The committee said their insights left policymakers "better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy." The academy said the models are now used by central banks and governments around the world, and their work helped shape how central banks set interest rates and communicate policy.

The award comes as central banks confront energy-driven inflation and risks to economic growth, giving the recognition particular relevance to current policy debates. Both laureates are American-born academics.

stories.headline: 14-year-old arrested after shooting principal and teacher at school in southern France
stories.summary:
A 14-year-old student was arrested Monday after a principal and a teacher were shot at Lakanal middle school in Aubagne, southern France. Regional officials said the boy entered the school with a shotgun inside a guitar case and opened fire before a member of staff restrained him in a corridor.

The 53-year-old headteacher was reportedly shot in the leg and lower back, and the 37-year-old teacher was hit in the thigh. Their injuries are not life-threatening, and a third person sustained minor injuries. No children were harmed, and students were confined within seconds. A psychological support unit was set up for affected pupils.

Local media, citing sources familiar with the investigation, said the incident was not thought to be linked to ongoing protests over school conditions. Mayor Jean-Pierre Squillari said the father had requested a meeting with the school's educational advisor, but little else is known. Education Minister Edouard Geffray and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez were due to visit the scene, with Geffray calling the attack further evidence of the rise of unchecked violence in society.

stories.headline: Update: Iran Calls Latest U.S. Proposal to End War 'Insufficient' as Houthis Strike Riyadh Airport Again
stories.summary:
Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and a former Revolutionary Guard commander, said Tehran finds the latest U.S. response to its proposal to end the war "insufficient." Iranian state news agency IRNA carried his comments. Rezaei said Iran is no longer responding to Washington and that the United States must clarify certain issues, without giving details. He said the U.S. has accepted some of Iran's seven conditions while others remain unclear.

Rezaei also threatened "cables, data centers, AI facilities and other sites in the region" if intense fighting resumes. The Guard's navy warned that any ship in the Strait of Hormuz that turns off its navigation and identification systems would be "identified as hostile." Attacks on ships in the strait have increased since Iran's proposal, which echoed a memorandum of understanding that collapsed days after signing in June, was rejected last month. The two sides remain in contact through mediators.

Separately, a projectile struck the same passenger terminal at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport that was hit Saturday in an attack that killed 12 people. Saudi authorities reported new injuries. Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen claimed both attacks, and the airport has been targeted daily since Wednesday. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree urged "everyone to take our warnings seriously."

In Israel, former Attorney General Avichai Mandelblit took the witness stand in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial, with elections weeks away. Mandelblit, whom Netanyahu handpicked and who indicted him seven years ago for fraud, breach of trust and bribery, testified with Netanyahu present in the courtroom. Netanyahu denies any wrongdoing.

stories.headline: Hurricane Simon Batters Mexico's Pacific Coast as Category 3 Storm
stories.summary:
Hurricane Simon pounded Mexico's Pacific coast on Sunday as a Category 3 storm with winds of about 120 mph. It had earlier strengthened into a Category 4 hurricane while approaching the coast. Its most powerful winds and rain slammed communities between the Sierra Madre and the ocean.

The storm's eye remained offshore, with its center moving parallel to the coast and closing in on the Puerto Vallarta area. The most damaging winds and rain there were expected around midnight and to continue through Monday morning. Forecasters warned of life-threatening flooding in the resort city and surrounding areas.

The full extent of damage, casualties and power outages is not yet known. Further updates are expected as the storm passes and officials assess the impact along the coast.

stories.headline: Federal Judge Orders Halt to Taxpayer-Funded Trump Ads Weeks Before Midterms
stories.summary:
A federal judge on Sunday ordered the Trump administration to immediately stop taxpayer-funded advertisements featuring President Trump, saying the ads are likely unlawful. The order covers any commercials scheduled to air later in the day. It temporarily blocks the campaign weeks before November's midterm elections while multiple lawsuits over the administration's use of public money proceed.

The ruling stems from a suit in the Southern District of New York brought by the watchdog group Common Cause, the nonprofit Democracy Forward and other plaintiffs. The Department of Homeland Security tapped $20 million in taxpayer funds for the ads. The White House has defended them as public service announcements.

The administration had indicated the campaign was set to end Sunday, so it argued there was no need for the court to intervene. Critics of the ads contend they promote the president's political message with public money ahead of an election, while the administration maintains they serve a public informational purpose. Further proceedings in the case are expected.

stories.headline: Trump and Rubio Weigh Firing Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are considering firing U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle, according to a senior U.S. official who spoke Sunday. The deliberations follow a series of reports alleging she engaged in improper and possibly illegal conduct before and during her tenure in Athens.

The official said Trump and Rubio are "extremely pissed off" by her reported conduct and would likely decide soon. Guilfoyle faces mounting allegations in Greece, and Vice President JD Vance and Rubio have weighed in on the controversies surrounding the envoy.

No final decision has been announced. Guilfoyle has not been reported to have responded to the specific allegations in the material available. A dismissal would end the tenure of one of the president's closest political allies in a prominent diplomatic post.
